Some shares may have comments attached to them. The socialActions/comments API enables you to write and read comments on shares.
The service currently provides the following methods:

Get a Comment
Batch Get a Collection of Comments
Get Comments on Shares
Get Comments on Comments
Create a Comment
Edit a Comment
Delete a Comment
For reactions and social metadata on social actions on a post, please see Reactions and Social Metadata.

Rows.Text: Post, comment, and react on posts on behalf of an organization. Restricted to organizations in which the authenticated member has one of the following company page roles: ADMINISTRATORDIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTERRECRUITING_POSTER

Retrieve organizations' posts, comments, and reactions. Restricted to organizations in which the authenticated member has one of the following company page roles. ADMINISTRATORDIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER
Post, comment, and react on posts on behalf of an authenticated member.
Restricted Retrieve posts, reactions, and likes on behalf of an authenticated member. This permission is granted to select developers only.

Blocks.Text: For more information about company page roles, refer to Organization Access Control by role.
The socialActions endpoint provides comments API that allows access to both personal and organization comments. The type of URN specified in the actor field of a comment indicates the type:

Rows.Text: Comment was created by a member. The member is displayed as the publisher.
Comment was created by a member on behalf of an organizational entity. The organization or brand is displayed as the publisher.

Blocks.Text: A comment URN is a composite URN constructed using the ID of the comment and the URN of the thread the comment is on. For example, a comment with an ID of 6636062862760562688 on thread URN urn:li:activity:6631349431612559360 would look like - urn:li:comment:(urn:li:activity:6631349431612559360,6636062862760562688).

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/{shareUrn|ugcPostUrn|commentUrn}/comments/{commentId}

curl -X GET 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/{shareUrn|ugcPostUrn|commentUrn}/comments/{commentId}' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}'\
-H 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
-H 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0'

To resolve nested comments for a given parent comment, provide a parent commentUrn as the target in the request URL. A commentUrn is a composite URN constructed using a threadUrn such as an ActivityUrn and a comment ID.

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/urn:li:comment:(urn:li:activity:6273189577469632512,6275822846992351232)/comments

curl -X GET 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/urn:li:comment:(urn:li:activity:6273189577469632512,6275822846992351232)/comments' \

The table below lists commonly encountered errors retrieving social actions. It is not meant to be a comprehensive list of all possible social action retrieval errors.

Rows.Text: Invalid query parameters passed to request

Occurs when using Restli 2.0 and the query parameters are not encoded properly. See Protocol Version for more on Restli 2.0 encoding. Calls with Postman and some other HTTP clients can trigger this error. Try using curl or another client when testing.
Indicates an invalid URN was requested. Try again with a share or ugcPost URN.
Text of the comment. May contain attributes such as links to people and organizations.
The content of the comment, such as an image.
For nested comments, this is the URN of the parent comment. This is not available for first-level comments.

Blocks.Text: Use the object field in the request body to specify the share or the ugcPost which contains the comment. Specify the share or the ugcPost in the request URL, and represent it as an URN.

Use the ID returned in the response header to take further action on the newly created comment. The following response body also contains a comment URN which can be used as parent comment for creating nested comments.

http


curl
POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/{shareUrn|ugcPostUrn|commentUrn}/comments
Note
For more information on how to upload an image and obtain the image URN required here, see the Image API documentation.

Only when editing comment as an organization

Blocks.Text: Only the text and attributes field in the comment's message field may be modified.

http


curl
POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/{shareUrn|ugcPostUrn}/comments/{comment ID}?actor={actorURN}
x-resourceidentity-urn: urn:li:comment:(urn:li:activity:6912417282191147008,6915442672119734272)

This is a composite URN constructed from the target in the request URL and the comment ID. Therefore, the URN in this header is not a reliable identifier for the comment. An accurate key for a comment can always be constructed from the comment's object field (which may differ from the target in the request URL) and its ID.

Blocks.Text: Comment text may contain attributes, which are links to other LinkedIn entities such as people or organizations. Mentioning requires knowledge of the URN for the referenced entity. You must also specify the part of the comment text that should be rendered as a link to the entity.

Rows.Text: The length of the annotation link
The starting character index beginning the annotation link
An object that includes the URN of the organization or member you want to mention in the comment.

Blocks.Text: An entity field is now part of the content field in a comment, replacing the url field. When creating a comment with an image, specify the image as an image URN within the entity field instead of the URL field. This ImageUrn is obtained when uploading an image to the Vector API (if an Urn like urn:li:digitalMediaAsset:ABC123 is returned then use urn:li:image:ABC123). Learn more.

Rows.Text: The Digitalmedia Asset URN of the image you want to include in the comment.
The type of the content, in this case, use "IMAGE". (This is a read-only field and shouldn't be provided for comment creates.)
